# Phase 34.4 native-host scripted answers

Use equivalent briefs under `claude -p` and `codex exec --sandbox workspace-write`.
When the inherited approval mode is automatic review, use `codex exec --approve-for-me`
instead: this CLI option itself selects workspace-write plus automatic review and
is mutually exclusive with `--sandbox`. Record the resolved authority and each review.
Each arm starts in a fresh scratch repository. Record the exact executable, version,
argv, source commit, plugin manifest digest, scratch identity, and `AuthorityEnvelope`.
The authority is filesystem `workspace-write`, network `inherited`, approvals `inherited`.
Permission or sandbox bypass options are forbidden. Do not widen inherited authority,
write outside scratch, contact product remotes, or perform unrecorded external actions.

## Common answers

Project: greenfield-proof. TypeScript library/CLI; npm; mobile: none; non-Blade.
Audience: developers importing a greeting function and invoking its CLI. The first
release exports a typed greeting and CLI with passing tests. No authentication,
external service, deployment, or product remote. Preserve unknowns explicitly.
Use the installed greenfield and roadmap plugin contracts and library-cli manifest.
Read the templates and references; do not substitute invented config keys or omit
promised homes. Existing brownfield homes and generated harness blocks are immutable.

## First invocation: proposal only

Read the fixture and run only the named `roadmap config capabilities --json`
compatibility command. Do not invoke `roadmap init` in any form, including
`roadmap init --help`, before approval. Read static source or top-level help for
syntax. Do not write or run a generator. Produce a complete Artifact / Target / Reason proposal, including every
command, dependency/network action, home, gate, and catalog repair. Also emit one
JSON object `{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[],"commands":[],"gates":{}}` with
concrete populated values. Its gates have exactly lint, types, unit, integration,
build, e2e, emit. Each non-none gate has an executable command; each absent gate has
a reason. Validate those keys before requesting approval. Do not emit an approval
event yourself. Stop and await the next invocation.

The command plan is executable evidence. Each `commands` entry has the exact
absolute scratch `cwd`, a complete shell `command`, and an explicit `network`
description. Include full heredoc contents, generator/install/init calls, checks,
and wrapped gates; no pseudocode, omitted writer bodies, or placeholders. The
seven proposed gate strings must exactly match the config produced after approval.
During execution, run every planned shell command exactly once, in proposal order, and successfully,
with `cd '<scratch>' &&` followed by the unchanged proposed command. Do not add
shell discovery/checks or combine/split approved commands. Put discovery before
proposal or in the separate read-only audit. Read/Glob/Grep tools may inspect files.
All writes must use the explicitly proposed shell commands through Bash or
exec_command; Write, Edit, apply_patch, and other implicit file mutation tools are
not part of this trial's approved execution protocol. New-file writers use exclusive
creation; edits verify approved before-digests and reject unsafe/symlink targets.

For Codex execution, use direct `exec_command` calls or only this orchestration
form, with strict JSON argument objects: `text(await tools.exec_command({...}));`.
Use one call per envelope, quoted JSON keys, and no variables, aliases, other tools,
or arbitrary JavaScript. If polling is needed, the only other permitted envelope
is `text(await tools.write_stdin({...}));` with empty `chars`; it cannot send input.
The actual `cmd` is the exact proposed command with the explicit scratch cwd prefix.
Set `workdir` to scratch; do not request a custom shell or a TTY.
A required scoped automatic-review request may use `sandbox_permissions` and its
justification in that JSON object; it may not widen the requested operation.

## Driver approval and execution

The driver checks the complete proposal and unchanged initial tree, then records the
approval response: `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN` as a separate input event.
Resume the same host session with that exact standalone input. The prior proposal
is the approved path/command allowlist; do not bundle new instructions into approval.
If the proposal fails validation, issue no approval and capture the failed arm.
If any preapproval mutation occurs, STOP immediately without deleting or reverting
it. Only the outer evidence driver may quarantine the failed scratch tree; an
agent cleanup cannot erase the failure.

Execute only approved operations. Emit `WRITE:` prose diagnostics for traceability (not extra shell calls), but
success requires raw native tool events and independently observed file snapshots;
model-authored diagnostics alone are insufficient. Run every non-none gate separately with explicit `cd '<scratch>' &&` cwd evidence.
Use the host envelope below for suite/build/type commands; retain both the exact
portable configured command and the wrapped native invocation with its real exit. Here `<scratch>` is the absolute observed
consumer directory and `<configured command>` is its exact config binding. Stop on permission denial,
missing sibling, invalid schema, changed existing home, or failing command.

Required empty artifacts include PRD, both ADRs, CODE-STYLE, architecture index,
UX canon, harness adapters, README, archetype outputs, catalog checker, and the one
resolved roadmap config. Brownfield receipts separately account for each missing
home, preserve original homes byte-identically, and mechanically constrain the diff
to approved gaps. Test migrated docs/roadmap, explicit root override, and ambiguous
dual-marked roots without creating a second configuration.

## Repeated invocation

second run: audit the completed tree. Require zero proposals, zero writes, and an
identical final tree hash. Emit exactly one native assistant JSON result
`{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only if the audit
finds no remaining gaps; retain actual findings otherwise. Record a separate raw
transcript and tool events. Generate
the human report from validated receipts only. Missing, failed, stale, copied, or
incomplete native evidence remains blocking; never author a replacement receipt.

## Source and evidence driver

Freeze all source inputs before starting the four fresh arms. Obtain the invocation
base and complete dirty/untracked source digest from
`plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-evidence-source.mjs`.
Pass `sourceRoot`, `invocationBaseCommit`, and `sourceSnapshotSha256` in every
observer request alongside `scratch`, `evidence`, `argv`, `stage`, and `timeout`.
Use `greenfield-native-observer.py` in the same directory to launch each request;
it checks source before and after and records transient filesystem mutations.
Keep `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` so read-only Git inspection does not refresh the index.
Propose scratch-local `.npm-cache/` and `.npm-logs/` paths when npm needs them;
include those settings in approved commands. Do not commit inside native fixtures.

After each stage finishes, run `greenfield-native-driver.mjs capture <host>
<stage-directory>` before resuming. The driver copies the native session and
checks identity, authority, command events, snapshots, and proposal structure.
Use separate `proposal`, `execution`, and `rerun` directories below each arm's
`dry-runs/evidence/` directory; never overwrite a failed attempt. Supply `arm.json`
with `host`, `kind`, absolute `scratchRoot`, unique `scratchIdentity`, discovered
`executable`, actual `version`, and brownfield `existingHomePaths`.
After all stages, `greenfield-native-driver.mjs project <empty-claude-arm>
<empty-codex-arm> <brownfield-claude-arm> <brownfield-codex-arm>` validates the
full proof before writing receipts and their Markdown projection. Angle-bracket
arguments denote the four retained arm directories, in the displayed order.
Missing evidence or any failed assertion blocks projection.

## Fixture-selected catalog check

Select the comparator before launching, using `selectCatalogCheck` from the native
evidence module and the reconciliation owner `skills/brownfield-audit/references/readme-reconcile.md`
(relative to the installed greenfield plugin root). For the empty `library-cli`
fixture, bind prospective project-root mode and project name `greenfield-proof`;
verify the generated package identity after execution. For the existing Nx fixture,
bind `node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --catalog emitted/repo-catalog.json`
and the existing emitted catalog's byte digest. A workspace wrapper package name
is not the identity of its multiple catalog projects. Refuse missing/malformed
required catalogs; preserve the selected catalog bytes throughout the arm.
Persist `catalogCheck` identically in arm metadata and every observer request.
Include its exact command once in the native proposal and run that comparator once
successfully after approval. Do not run the other mode or report an expected failure
as validation. Retain the selected source file with the other observed artifacts.

## Host build envelope

Resolve `/home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild` and its canonical path before launch;
bind its SHA-256, default limits, and permitted host effects as `gateWrapper` in
arm metadata and every stage request. Use the same binding for all four arms.
Keep `capbuild` out of consumer `gateCommands`; it is a host execution requirement,
not consumer tooling. For each build, type, unit, integration, and emit command,
propose its actual execution separately using this exact envelope:

```sh
cd '<scratch>' && /home/patrik/.local/bin/capbuild --env npm_config_cache=<scratch>/.npm-cache --env npm_config_logs_dir=<scratch>/.npm-logs <configured-command>
```

Define `<scratch>` as the absolute observed fixture root and `<configured-command>`
as its exact portable gate binding. Use literal absolute cache/log values. Select
portable gate commands without shell operators or assignment prefixes; use
`env TSX_DISABLE_CACHE=1 node --import tsx roadmap/lib/emit.ts` for the fixture emit
gate so transform caching stays disabled across the systemd environment boundary.
Do not change memory/swap/heap/slice defaults, disable locks, add arbitrary environment
options, or run an unwrapped suite inside a compound verification command. Keep
config check and the selected catalog comparator as separate ordinary invocations.

Permit only capbuild's inherited host-control effects outside the consumer tree:
transient user-systemd units and `/run/user/<uid>/capbuild-locks`, where `<uid>` is
the current numeric user id recorded by the driver. These are safety metadata;
they do not authorize any additional consumer path. Record the actual wrapper
command/output/exit and verify the bound executable digest remains unchanged.
The observer clears ambient capbuild, Node, and forwarded test overrides before
launch and records the cleared variable names without exposing their values.

---
name: using-zeroh-greenfield
description: Route requests phrased as init, scaffold, brownfield audit, fill gaps, or stack choice to the owning zeroh-greenfield skill.
---

# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |

# PRD interview

Ask one question at a time. Accept `Don't know yet` without filling in an
answer or inventing a decision. Preserve the user's words in the proposal.

| Interview field | Destination |
| --- | --- |
| Product | docs/PRD.md §Product |
| Audience | docs/PRD.md §Audience |

===== design-system.md
# Design-system step

Choose after the stack ruling and before generation. Record the choice in the
design ADR, UX canon, and roadmap pointers; never invent brand values.

## Web

Use shadcn/ui with Tailwind v4 and its CSS-first configuration. The proposal
must name the component sources and license tier before installation.

Use this `components.json` shape, replacing registry names only with approved
open registries:

```json
{
  "style": "new-york",
  "baseColor": "neutral",
  "cssVariables": true,
  "iconLibrary": "lucide",
  "registries": {
    "@magicui": "https://magicui.design/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

Keep one token source and generate the CSS variable projection from it. The byte-check guard fails when generated CSS bytes differ from the token source projection.

Capture `fonts | palette | spacing | ux-canon` as inputs to the UX home. Use
`external-assets-licensing.md §The tiers` to classify every external source.

## beautifului.dev — MIT — Allowed anywhere

beautifului.dev may supply cited copy-paste AI-interface primitives or an
approved registry item. Record provenance with the component proposal.

## Mobile mappings

| stack | mapping | UX inputs | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| shadcn_flutter | Share semantic token names with web and project them to Dart | ux-canon fonts palette spacing | shadcn_flutter |
| Material 3 | Translate semantic roles to Material theme tokens | ux-canon fonts palette spacing | https://m3.material.io |
| react-native-reusables | Project semantic tokens to React Native primitives | ux-canon fonts palette spacing | @react-native-reusables/cli |

## Blade handoff

Invoke `zeroh-design:blade-design` using Path 2. It owns selection and token
values. Store only these approved outputs:

- `designHomes.ux.bindingDesignSystem` points to the sibling-owned theme.
- The `ux-canon pointer line` names that binding without copying tokens.
- The design-system `ADR line` records the choice and owner.

If zeroh-design is absent, print `/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP.
===== archetypes/README.md
# Archetype manifest contract

## Generator
One fenced block containing a literal generator command.

## Post-steps
Exact approved edits after generation.

## File tree
One fenced, non-empty two-level tree.

## Conventions delta
Only archetype-specific additions to the shared conventions.

## testConventions
At least two literal commands or patterns.

## designHomes
The architecture and UX pointers consumed by the roadmap.

## Verify
Exactly one fenced, single-line exit-code command. Keep observations and dates
only in `VERIFY-RECORD-2026-09.md`.
===== archetypes/library-cli.md
## Generator
```sh
npx create-vite@^8 my-lib --template vanilla-ts
```

Source: https://vite.dev/guide/. Vite is MIT, tier `Allowed anywhere`.

## Post-steps
Install `tsup: ^8.5` and `@types/node`, and include `node` in the TypeScript
`types` list. tsup is sourced from https://tsup.egoist.dev/; it is MIT and
`Allowed anywhere`. Set package.json `exports` to `./dist/index.js`, `bin` to
`./dist/cli.js`, and `files` to `dist`. Configure `tsup.config.ts` with
`entry: ['src/index.ts', 'src/cli.ts']`, `format: ['esm']`, and `dts: true`.
Set the package.json `build` script to `tsup`.
Give the CLI a Node shebang and a stable `--help` path. Add at least one
`node:test` file for the public API, then run the tsup build before Verify.

## File tree
```text
my-lib/
my-lib/package.json
my-lib/src/index.ts
my-lib/src/cli.ts
my-lib/tsup.config.ts
```

## Conventions delta
Keep the reusable API in `src/index.ts` and the thin executable adapter in
`src/cli.ts`; publish only built artifacts through `exports`, `bin`, and `files`.

## testConventions
Use `node --test` for behavior and `node dist/cli.js --help` as the built CLI
smoke check. Test runner source: https://nodejs.org/api/test.html.

## designHomes
Set `designHomes.architecture.home` to `docs/architecture.md` and
`designHomes.ux.canon` to `docs/ux-canon.md`.

## Verify
```sh
test -f my-lib/package.json && test -f my-lib/src/index.ts && test -f my-lib/src/cli.ts && test -f my-lib/tsup.config.ts && (cd my-lib && npm run build && node --test && node dist/cli.js --help && node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --project-root .)
```

## CI and release adapter

Select `library-cli` in `.github/greenfield-delivery.json` and follow
[the shared CI/release strategy](../ci-release-strategy.md) for its exact inventory,
executor, raw report, coverage merge and build contract. Bind runner/build argv
into the shard manifest before execution; require exact-once leaf/file selection.
Generate `scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and
`.github/workflows/release.yml` only from the approved preservation plan.
Missing tooling/reporters are unavailable with the adapter install remedy.
Affected PR checks backstop into authoritative full shards on main/manual runs;
release promotes the same verified artifact bytes without rebuilding.
===== standards.md
## Proposal and approval
Before writing, present `file | source facts | planned sections` for every target and wait for approval. The approved interview, selected archetype, and `design-gate.md` are the only source facts.

## AGENTS.md
AGENTS.md is the sole conventions home. Fill `## Conventions`, `## Don’t`, and `## Generalize-forward`; require Flag-first delivery and keep release-only work in `hold[]`.

## Harness pointers
CLAUDE.md contains `@AGENTS.md` plus harness-only lines. Other harness files point to AGENTS.md and never copy conventions.

## Generated blocks
Preserve generated blocks byte-for-byte, including everything from `<!-- nx configuration start -->` through `<!-- nx configuration end -->`.

## CODE-STYLE.md
Derive code style from the repository's lint and format configuration; do not invent another standard.

## Architecture index
Index the approved architecture records and link to their canonical homes.

## UX canon
Link the UX canon to its design token home from `references/design-system.md`.

`entry: ['src/index.ts', 'src/cli.ts']`, `format: ['esm']`, and `dts: true`.
Set the package.json `build` script to `tsup`.
Give the CLI a Node shebang and a stable `--help` path. Add at least one

## File tree

```text
my-lib/
my-lib/package.json
my-lib/src/index.ts
my-lib/src/cli.ts
my-lib/tsup.config.ts
```

Keep the reusable API in `src/index.ts` and the thin executable adapter in

Missing tooling/reporters are unavailable with the adapter install remedy.
Affected PR checks backstop into authoritative full shards on main/manual runs;
release promotes the same verified artifact bytes without rebuilding.

===== ci-release-strategy.md
# CI and exact-artifact release

Use the consumer-owned `scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs` as the sole lifecycle engine.
Copy its two workflows to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and `release.yml` only after
approval. Configure `.github/greenfield-delivery.json`; missing configuration,
runner, report parser, baseline, credential or provider is unavailable and exits
nonzero with an install/configuration remedy. A template is not a successful run.

## Approval and configuration

Present the selected adapter, exact inventory/test/build argv, setup commands,
report paths, coverage roots, shard count, count/coverage baselines, affected PR
command, main branch, retention, protected environment and provider placeholders.
Pin dependency versions in the consumer lockfile. Preserve existing workflows;
collisions require an explicit reviewed merge. Never invent credentials or a
working deployment. Provider defaults to unavailable; no arbitrary promotion hook
is accepted. The optional selected provider is `aws-s3-v1`, configured with
`environment`, `bucket`, `region`, `keyPrefix` and an approved OIDC `roleArn`.
The bucket must support versioning and SHA-256 checksums. Other providers require
a separately implemented and verified adapter before use.

Configuration version 1 has `archetype`, `setupArgv` (array of exact argv arrays),
`affectedArgv` (an argv array with a standalone `{base}` token), `shardCount`,
`evidenceDays` (1 through 7), `baseline: {minTests,minUnits,coverageFloor}`,
`adapterConfig: {maxInfraRetries,coverageRoots,leafTasks}`, `runners`, `build`
and `release`. `operationalRoots` explicitly lists dependency/cache/report roots
(defaults `.ci` and `node_modules`); it is also bound in the plan. Each runner binds `inventoryArgv`, `inventoryFormat`, optional
`filePattern`/`pathPrefix`/`targetSuffix`, `shardArgv`, optional reporter `env`,
and `rawReports: [{path,format,from?}]`. Vitest/Playwright also require
`selectionArgv` and `selectionFormat`: the actual pre-run selected file inventory
must equal the single requested unit, or execution stops. `from: stdout` retains the actual process
output as a raw report. Substitutions are whole argv data, never shell evaluation:
`{unit}`, `{reportDir}`, `{junit}`, `{coverage}`. Build binds `argv` and explicit
`outputs` roots; symlinks and overlapping output roots are rejected. The planner
binds the complete runner/build execution contract into `adapterConfigDigest`.
Changing a runner, reporter, output or build command after planning fails.
Production preparation and run/build boundaries verify the exact Git SHA/tree and
an unchanged source snapshot, including ignored/untracked files. Setup/tests may
change only the declared operational roots; build may additionally change its
declared output roots. Other tracked or untracked changes fail.

## Six adapters

Atomic identity is exactly `{runner,canonicalPathOrLeafTask}`. Keep distinct runner
populations disjoint even if two runners reference the same filename. The adapter
owns inventory argv, execution argv, raw formats, canonical coverage merge and
build. The following argv are baseline contracts to fill with the consumer's
approved reporter configuration; missing reporter output is a hard failure.

| Archetype | Identity / exact inventory | Executor / raw reports / build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web | `vitest` canonical files from `npm exec -- vitest list --filesOnly`; independently `playwright` canonical files from `npm exec -- playwright test --list --reporter=json` | Vitest run with the approved exact-file selector, `--reporter=junit --outputFile={junit} --coverage --coverage.reporter=lcov --coverage.reportsDirectory={reportDir}`; Playwright exact-file selection with `--retries=0 --reporter=junit`, `PLAYWRIGHT_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}` and approved LCOV collection. JUnit + LCOV; canonical line merge; `npm run build`. |
| expo | `jest` canonical files from `npm exec -- jest --listTests --json`; separately the same Playwright inventory as web | `npm exec -- jest --runInBand --runTestsByPath {unit} --reporters=default --reporters=jest-junit --coverage --coverageReporters=lcov --coverageDirectory={reportDir}`; `JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}`. Independent Playwright runner as above. JUnit + LCOV; canonical merge; `npm exec -- expo export`. |
| flutter | `flutter` canonical `_test.dart` files from `git ls-files -z -- test`, filtered by `_test\\.dart$` | `flutter test --machine --coverage --coverage-path={coverage} {unit}`; retain stdout as `flutter-machine`, plus LCOV. Canonical merge; approved `flutter build web` or the selected platform's exact build argv. |
| android | `gradle` leaf tasks such as `:app:testDebugUnitTest`, discovered from the actual Gradle task inventory and dependency graph | `./gradlew {unit} --no-daemon --console=plain` with selected JUnit XML and JaCoCo XML outputs. Configure the actual leaf `Test` task/report output and coverage finalizer; declare its dependencies in `leafTasks`. Reject aggregate tasks and overlapping task dependency sets. Canonical merge; approved `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease --no-daemon`. |
| nx-monorepo | `nx` leaf project-target identities such as `package-a:test`, inventory `npm exec -- nx show projects --withTarget=test --json` plus configured target suffix; inspect actual target/dependency metadata | `npm exec -- nx run {unit} --excludeTaskDependencies --skipNxCache`; each approved leaf runner emits JUnit + LCOV (or explicitly selected supported raw formats). Never infer one reporter from another executor. Reject aggregates/dependency overlap. Canonical merge; `npm exec -- nx run-many -t build` with approved explicit artifact roots. |
| library-cli | `node:test` canonical files from `git ls-files -z -- test tests`, filtered by the selected test filename convention | `node --test --experimental-test-coverage --test-reporter=junit --test-reporter-destination={junit} --test-reporter=lcov --test-reporter-destination={coverage} {unit}`. JUnit + LCOV; canonical merge; `npm run build`. |

Vitest/Playwright positional filters can match more than one file. The approved
runner binding must use an exact selector and prove its selected inventory equals
the one requested identity before execution; a broad pattern is not an exact
selector. Playwright browser coverage is not automatic: install and configure the
approved instrumented coverage reporter, or report the adapter unavailable. Do
not substitute an empty coverage file. For Gradle/Nx, the inventory command must
produce an unambiguous leaf list; unsupported inventory/report formats require an
approved converter that consumes actual tool output, never a hand-maintained
success list. SDK/JDK/browser setup belongs in reviewed `setupArgv`, with pinned
versions and no secret defaults. `ADAPTERS` in the engine names install remedies.

## Determinism and completeness

Versioned manifests bind source SHA, tree, normalized sorted unique identities,
runner/build contract digest and inventory digest. Normalize Windows separators
to `/`; reject traversal, absolute paths and duplicate identities. Generate the
inventory afresh: renamed identities replace old names, deleted tests disappear
and therefore face the approved count baseline. Default weight is exactly 1;
round-robin count balancing is deterministic. One shard and more requested shards
than units are valid; clamp the latter to units and emit no empty shard. Input
permutation cannot change the manifest, shards or digest. Fan-in requires every
planned shard exactly once and its executed identity union exactly equal to the
inventory. Report paths/digests are retained, not accepted from a summary alone.

The engine parses JUnit XML, Flutter machine JSON lines, LCOV and JaCoCo XML with
separate parsers. Truncated/contradictory summaries, duplicate cases, hidden failed
or skipped cases, malformed coverage, unknown formats and missing outputs fail.
Coverage paths are remapped only through approved roots, then merged once by
canonical file/line (maximum hit count, never summing percentages). Coverage is a
line-coverage floor in version 1; branch/function percentages are not asserted.

Keep every attempt. The generated runner disables test retries. Bounded external
infrastructure retry allows at most `maxInfraRetries` (0 by default, at most 2),
requires explicit infrastructure code/reason and retains first-attempt evidence.
A required test failure remains blocking even if a rerun passes (flaky).
Quarantine requires owner, reason and unexpired expiry, and still blocks an
authoritative release. Missing first attempts or gaps in numbering fail. Upload
compact reports and raw failure diagnostics under `always()`, even on failed jobs.

`minTests`, `minUnits` and `coverageFloor` are approved baselines. During preparation,
the engine reads the previous baseline from the tracked delivery config at `BASE_SHA`:
push uses the event's previous-main SHA; manual full requires an explicit approved
`base_sha` input. Scheduled/local validation uses the current commit's first parent.
A nonempty base must be an exact ancestor preceding HEAD. Missing history fails;
a root commit or new-branch push can prove that no prior branch baseline exists.
The plan binds `{baseSha,baseline,baselineDigest,requestedDigest}` as
`adapterConfig.baselineReference`, carried through fan-in and release verification.
A changed baseline requires
`baselineApproval: {baseSha,previous,previousDigest,approvedDigest,owner,reason}`,
matching the derived previous baseline and proposed values. The approval's `previous`
value never supplies the source of truth. First installation requires the same
approval with `bootstrap:true`, `previous:null`, and the digest of null as
`previousDigest`, bound to the proven absent config/base and approved current floor.
Record that bootstrap decision in the init proposal; it is not advance write approval.
Never lower a floor to hide a regression. Review baseline changes like code; a digest
is a binding, not an independent human authorization mechanism.

## Lifecycle and release proof

PRs run the configured affected command using the exact base SHA. Main and manual
full runs inventory, plan, execute shards, fan in, build once and attest. Nightly
runs diagnose with the same full tests/build but do not publish authoritative
release evidence. PR cancellation is enabled; full/release runs never cancel one
another. The authoritative artifact name includes source SHA and producer run ID.

The manifest is `{schemaVersion,authoritative,sha,tree,suiteManifestDigest,
shardReports,coverageDigest,buildDigest,producerRunId,expiresAt,baselineDigest,
testCount,coveragePercent}`. Each raw shard report has a digest. Build files are
regular files encoded in a canonical content-addressed bundle; the build digest
binds paths and exact bytes. The attestation signs the manifest, transitively
binding all test, coverage and build evidence. GitHub's signature verification is
separate from the local digest checks.

Release resolves a tag/manual reference to an exact commit and tree, enumerates
successful full producers, downloads evidence and requires exactly one unexpired
same-SHA authoritative producer. It verifies the signed manifest against the
repository, signer workflow and source digest, then recomputes every local link.
Missing/expired/ambiguous evidence, changed tags, report/inventory/coverage/build
or producer drift is red. The verification handoff retains SHA, tree, suite digest and complete build-record
digest. Protected promotion re-verifies expiry/tag/tree and
uploads only the already-verified bundle; no build or consumer command runs there.
The fixed AWS adapter obtains an OIDC token, assumes the approved role, uploads
with a SHA-256 checksum, and checks the versioned provider readback checksum and
size. Missing credentials, unsupported provider, skipped upload or mismatched
readback is red.

All actions use immutable full commit pins with version comments. Workflow-level
permissions are empty; test/build jobs get contents-read only. The isolated
non-PR, non-nightly CI signing job alone gets attestations-write and OIDC for
signing. In release, only the protected deployment job gets OIDC. Forks receive no
secrets. Artifacts expire within 7 days (raw diagnostics 3; verified promotion 1).
Replace the environment placeholder only with the approved protected environment.

## Validation and sources

Mandatory: repository-pinned js-yaml 3.15.2 parses both workflows, then executable
workflow simulations invoke the shipped CLI through actual YAML `run` snippets.
Mocks exist only at external executable/artifact/provider boundaries. Mutation
checks cover missing/duplicate/red/retried/quarantined/malformed evidence,
stale/expired/ambiguous producers, count/coverage floors, every digest link, moved
tags, changed argv and rebuild attempts. Optional actionlint was absent on the
phase-34 validation host; it cannot replace these checks. That host's older `gh`
also lacks attestation commands; a real release runner must have current GitHub
CLI support, otherwise release stops with its tool error.

Commands and pins checked 2026-09-05 against official sources:
[Node test runner](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html),
[Vitest CLI](https://vitest.dev/guide/cli.html),
[Playwright CLI](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli),
[Flutter testing](https://docs.flutter.dev/testing/overview),
[Gradle test reports](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/java_testing.html),
[Nx CLI](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-commands),
[GitHub attestations](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations),
[gh attestation verification](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify).
Action SHA/version pairs were resolved with `git ls-remote --tags` against the
corresponding official `github.com/actions/<action>` repositories, including the
peeled commit for annotated attestation tags.
===== pointers.md
## Tool gate
The skill's first preflight must prove `scope-manifest-json-v1` plus scoped,
affected, and impacted slots before this reference is used.

## Config branch
Use the canonical discovery procedure in `skills/brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md` to locate the resolved root before testing configuration presence. If its config is absent, propose `roadmap init`; if present, never run init. Merge only approved missing keys. Existing keys are preserved unless an individually approved stale/partial repair names the old value, replacement, and evidence. Never create a second config at the repository top level.

## Bind and prove commands
The tables are proposal inputs, not proof that a generator installed a runner.
Before approval, inspect the generated or existing package scripts, test files,
Gradle tasks, and tool availability. Propose installation/configuration of missing
promised runners and at least one meaningful test. Never bind `npm test` or
Playwright without that setup. A slot with no applicable tooling is explicitly
`none` (declared absent), with a recorded reason approved in the proposal; absence
is not a passing test. Never downgrade an existing or promised test to `none` to
make verification green. Replace candidate bindings with the repository's actual
commands where needed and retain their source evidence.
Execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer project root after approval and
record its command, cwd, and exit. STOP on failure or unavailable tooling; config

## Delivery proposal, copy and validation

release environment. The supplied workflows support GitHub Actions; another
provider is unavailable until its adapter is implemented and approved. Present
all commands, baselines, setup/cache roots and provider placeholders. Do not

```json
{"delivery":{"provider":"github-actions","adapter":"library-cli","configPath":".github/greenfield-delivery.json","workflowPaths":[".github/workflows/ci.yml",".github/workflows/release.yml"],"plannerPath":"scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs","releaseEnvironment":"<approved-protected-environment>","collision":{"existingPaths":[],"decision":"create","preserveUntilApproval":true,"mergeManifests":{}},"validationCommands":[{"command":"<complete-installed-output-validation-command>","cwd":"<absolute-consumer-root>"}]}}
```

merged additions. STOP if no explicit merge decision is available. The complete

merge; no other collision is authorized. Existing workflow bytes remain untouched

prior job; sorted `preservedTopLevel` names every unchanged non-jobs top-level key.

and `after` values. List every original full comment/marker line, with original
whitespace and order, in `preservedComments` and retain those lines byte-for-byte.

Use an empty `mergeManifests` object when there are no existing workflows.
Brownfield audit consumes this same owner contract for its
missing/partial delivery rows; do not duplicate the interview or lifecycle.

After approval, copy `templates/scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs` byte-for-byte to
`scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs`, then copy/fill `templates/github/workflows/ci.yml`
and `release.yml` into `.github/workflows/`. Merge approved existing jobs and
preserve their exact content. Write `.github/greenfield-delivery.json` with the
selected adapter, complete runner/build bindings and approved baseline. Replace
the release workflow's environment placeholder with the approved protected
environment, retaining least privilege. Leave `release.provider` as `none` when
no deployment provider was selected; this explicitly blocks promotion without
claiming a deployment passed.

Set `testCadence.enabled: true` and `testCadence.backstop` to
`.github/workflows/ci.yml (authoritative full suite on main/manual runs)`; merge
existing values only with the approved exact delta. Keep scoped/affected/impacted
bindings where actual tooling supports them. Populate README commands with the
same affected/local/full lifecycle and exact `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and
`.github/workflows/release.yml` paths. README catalog reconciliation still applies.

`greenfield-ci-release.test.mjs` supports `GREENFIELD_DELIVERY_ROOT=<consumer>`;
its mandatory pinned js-yaml parser reads the installed workflows and its
executable simulations import/copy the installed planner. Run its complete suite
(no test-name filter) and require terminal TAP totals with zero failure,
cancellation or skipped tests. Preserve the real native command ID/exit and
record the optional actionlint path/version or `ACTIONLINT_UNAVAILABLE`. A
passed simulation is not a published GitHub run or a live cloud deployment.

For phase validation, bind the exact host command in `delivery.validationCommands`:
`<bound-capbuild-executable> --env GREENFIELD_DELIVERY_ROOT=<consumer>
node --test <installed-roadmap>/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-ci-release.test.mjs`.
The host wrapper is validation infrastructure; never embed its machine path in
portable consumer gateCommands. The suite creates isolated temporary fixtures
and simulates external SDK/provider boundaries, then cleans them up. Preserve
its inherited approval controls. A final read-only audit must propose no changes
and write nothing; it must not rerun mutation-producing tests during that audit.

## Native proof of optional Nx gates

The phase-validation proposal keeps its seven required base slots in `gates` and
adds the schema-supported slots in `optionalGates`. Nx installation includes
`unit-scoped`, `unit-affected` and `unit-impacted`; never omit them to fit a
seven-key evidence record. Generated `gateCommands` equals the exact union.

For each template slot, propose one `optionalGateRuns[slot]` record with
`substitutions: {manifest: "@<absolute-in-scratch-manifest>"}` or
`substitutions: {range: "<exact-base-SHA>..<exact-head-SHA>"}`, and `inputSha256`
hashing the raw manifest bytes or literal range. Use a separate approved regular
JSON file for each manifest: `{protocol:"scope-manifest-json-v1",paths:[...]}`
with sorted unique real repository-relative files. A scoped manifest contains
actual test files; an affected manifest includes a source file. List these inputs
as explicit proposal artifacts. The driver may prepare two real fixture commits
before observation; native initialization never changes fixture history.

Execute each optional slot separately using the literal single substitution in
its configured command. For Nx the command is `node scripts/run-nx-test-tier.mjs
'{manifest}'` or `'{range}'`, with `env NX_DAEMON=false` when daemon writes must
be disabled. For a range, also execute `git rev-parse HEAD` and
`git diff --name-only -z <exact-range>` plus
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <base-SHA> <head-SHA>` to prove the current commit,
changed files and ancestry. Record the configured template, exact native command, substitution, input
digest, cwd, native tool-call ID and numeric exit. Require the actual selector's
scoped/affected tier and real test success; an unavailable or full fallback is
reported honestly and cannot stand in for the requested scoped proof.

approval. Configure `.github/greenfield-delivery.json`; missing configuration,

nonzero with an install/configuration remedy. A template is not a successful run.

## Approval and configuration

Present the selected adapter, exact inventory/test/build argv, setup commands,
report paths, coverage roots, shard count, count/coverage baselines, affected PR
command, main branch, retention, protected environment and provider placeholders.
Pin dependency versions in the consumer lockfile. Preserve existing workflows;
collisions require an explicit reviewed merge. Never invent credentials or a
working deployment. Provider defaults to unavailable; no arbitrary promotion hook
is accepted. The optional selected provider is `aws-s3-v1`, configured with
`environment`, `bucket`, `region`, `keyPrefix` and an approved OIDC `roleArn`.
The bucket must support versioning and SHA-256 checksums. Other providers require
a separately implemented and verified adapter before use.

Configuration version 1 has `archetype`, `setupArgv` (array of exact argv arrays),
`affectedArgv` (an argv array with a standalone `{base}` token), `shardCount`,
`evidenceDays` (1 through 7), `baseline: {minTests,minUnits,coverageFloor}`,
`adapterConfig: {maxInfraRetries,coverageRoots,leafTasks}`, `runners`, `build`
and `release`. `operationalRoots` explicitly lists dependency/cache/report roots
(defaults `.ci` and `node_modules`); it is also bound in the plan. Each runner binds `inventoryArgv`, `inventoryFormat`, optional
`filePattern`/`pathPrefix`/`targetSuffix`, `shardArgv`, optional reporter `env`,
and `rawReports: [{path,format,from?}]`. Vitest/Playwright also require
`selectionArgv` and `selectionFormat`: the actual pre-run selected file inventory
must equal the single requested unit, or execution stops. `from: stdout` retains the actual process
output as a raw report. Substitutions are whole argv data, never shell evaluation:
`{unit}`, `{reportDir}`, `{junit}`, `{coverage}`. Build binds `argv` and explicit
`outputs` roots; symlinks and overlapping output roots are rejected. The planner
binds the complete runner/build execution contract into `adapterConfigDigest`.
Changing a runner, reporter, output or build command after planning fails.
Production preparation and run/build boundaries verify the exact Git SHA/tree and
an unchanged source snapshot, including ignored/untracked files. Setup/tests may
change only the declared operational roots; build may additionally change its
declared output roots. Other tracked or untracked changes fail.

## Six adapters

Atomic identity is exactly `{runner,canonicalPathOrLeafTask}`. Keep distinct runner
populations disjoint even if two runners reference the same filename. The adapter
owns inventory argv, execution argv, raw formats, canonical coverage merge and
build. The following argv are baseline contracts to fill with the consumer's
approved reporter configuration; missing reporter output is a hard failure.

| Archetype | Identity / exact inventory | Executor / raw reports / build |
| --- | --- | --- |
| web | `vitest` canonical files from `npm exec -- vitest list --filesOnly`; independently `playwright` canonical files from `npm exec -- playwright test --list --reporter=json` | Vitest run with the approved exact-file selector, `--reporter=junit --outputFile={junit} --coverage --coverage.reporter=lcov --coverage.reportsDirectory={reportDir}`; Playwright exact-file selection with `--retries=0 --reporter=junit`, `PLAYWRIGHT_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}` and approved LCOV collection. JUnit + LCOV; canonical line merge; `npm run build`. |
| expo | `jest` canonical files from `npm exec -- jest --listTests --json`; separately the same Playwright inventory as web | `npm exec -- jest --runInBand --runTestsByPath {unit} --reporters=default --reporters=jest-junit --coverage --coverageReporters=lcov --coverageDirectory={reportDir}`; `JEST_JUNIT_OUTPUT_FILE={junit}`. Independent Playwright runner as above. JUnit + LCOV; canonical merge; `npm exec -- expo export`. |
| flutter | `flutter` canonical `_test.dart` files from `git ls-files -z -- test`, filtered by `_test\\.dart$` | `flutter test --machine --coverage --coverage-path={coverage} {unit}`; retain stdout as `flutter-machine`, plus LCOV. Canonical merge; approved `flutter build web` or the selected platform's exact build argv. |
| android | `gradle` leaf tasks such as `:app:testDebugUnitTest`, discovered from the actual Gradle task inventory and dependency graph | `./gradlew {unit} --no-daemon --console=plain` with selected JUnit XML and JaCoCo XML outputs. Configure the actual leaf `Test` task/report output and coverage finalizer; declare its dependencies in `leafTasks`. Reject aggregate tasks and overlapping task dependency sets. Canonical merge; approved `./gradlew :app:assembleRelease --no-daemon`. |
| nx-monorepo | `nx` leaf project-target identities such as `package-a:test`, inventory `npm exec -- nx show projects --withTarget=test --json` plus configured target suffix; inspect actual target/dependency metadata | `npm exec -- nx run {unit} --excludeTaskDependencies --skipNxCache`; each approved leaf runner emits JUnit + LCOV (or explicitly selected supported raw formats). Never infer one reporter from another executor. Reject aggregates/dependency overlap. Canonical merge; `npm exec -- nx run-many -t build` with approved explicit artifact roots. |
| library-cli | `node:test` canonical files from `git ls-files -z -- test tests`, filtered by the selected test filename convention | `node --test --experimental-test-coverage --test-reporter=junit --test-reporter-destination={junit} --test-reporter=lcov --test-reporter-destination={coverage} {unit}`. JUnit + LCOV; canonical merge; `npm run build`. |

Vitest/Playwright positional filters can match more than one file. The approved
runner binding must use an exact selector and prove its selected inventory equals
the one requested identity before execution; a broad pattern is not an exact
selector. Playwright browser coverage is not automatic: install and configure the
approved instrumented coverage reporter, or report the adapter unavailable. Do
not substitute an empty coverage file. For Gradle/Nx, the inventory command must
produce an unambiguous leaf list; unsupported inventory/report formats require an
approved converter that consumes actual tool output, never a hand-maintained
success list. SDK/JDK/browser setup belongs in reviewed `setupArgv`, with pinned
versions and no secret defaults. `ADAPTERS` in the engine names install remedies.

## Determinism and completeness

Versioned manifests bind source SHA, tree, normalized sorted unique identities,
runner/build contract digest and inventory digest. Normalize Windows separators
to `/`; reject traversal, absolute paths and duplicate identities. Generate the
inventory afresh: renamed identities replace old names, deleted tests disappear
and therefore face the approved count baseline. Default weight is exactly 1;
round-robin count balancing is deterministic. One shard and more requested shards
than units are valid; clamp the latter to units and emit no empty shard. Input
permutation cannot change the manifest, shards or digest. Fan-in requires every
planned shard exactly once and its executed identity union exactly equal to the
inventory. Report paths/digests are retained, not accepted from a summary alone.

The engine parses JUnit XML, Flutter machine JSON lines, LCOV and JaCoCo XML with
separate parsers. Truncated/contradictory summaries, duplicate cases, hidden failed
or skipped cases, malformed coverage, unknown formats and missing outputs fail.
Coverage paths are remapped only through approved roots, then merged once by
canonical file/line (maximum hit count, never summing percentages). Coverage is a
line-coverage floor in version 1; branch/function percentages are not asserted.

Keep every attempt. The generated runner disables test retries. Bounded external
infrastructure retry allows at most `maxInfraRetries` (0 by default, at most 2),
requires explicit infrastructure code/reason and retains first-attempt evidence.
A required test failure remains blocking even if a rerun passes (flaky).
Quarantine requires owner, reason and unexpired expiry, and still blocks an
authoritative release. Missing first attempts or gaps in numbering fail. Upload
compact reports and raw failure diagnostics under `always()`, even on failed jobs.

`minTests`, `minUnits` and `coverageFloor` are approved baselines. During preparation,
the engine reads the previous baseline from the tracked delivery config at `BASE_SHA`:
push uses the event's previous-main SHA; manual full requires an explicit approved
`base_sha` input. Scheduled/local validation uses the current commit's first parent.
A nonempty base must be an exact ancestor preceding HEAD. Missing history fails;
a root commit or new-branch push can prove that no prior branch baseline exists.
The plan binds `{baseSha,baseline,baselineDigest,requestedDigest}` as
`adapterConfig.baselineReference`, carried through fan-in and release verification.
A changed baseline requires
`baselineApproval: {baseSha,previous,previousDigest,approvedDigest,owner,reason}`,
matching the derived previous baseline and proposed values. The approval's `previous`
value never supplies the source of truth. First installation requires the same
approval with `bootstrap:true`, `previous:null`, and the digest of null as
`previousDigest`, bound to the proven absent config/base and approved current floor.
Record that bootstrap decision in the init proposal; it is not advance write approval.
Never lower a floor to hide a regression. Review baseline changes like code; a digest
is a binding, not an independent human authorization mechanism.

## Lifecycle and release proof

PRs run the configured affected command using the exact base SHA. Main and manual
full runs inventory, plan, execute shards, fan in, build once and attest. Nightly
runs diagnose with the same full tests/build but do not publish authoritative
release evidence. PR cancellation is enabled; full/release runs never cancel one
another. The authoritative artifact name includes source SHA and producer run ID.

The manifest is `{schemaVersion,authoritative,sha,tree,suiteManifestDigest,
shardReports,coverageDigest,buildDigest,producerRunId,expiresAt,baselineDigest,
testCount,coveragePercent}`. Each raw shard report has a digest. Build files are
regular files encoded in a canonical content-addressed bundle; the build digest
binds paths and exact bytes. The attestation signs the manifest, transitively
binding all test, coverage and build evidence. GitHub's signature verification is
separate from the local digest checks.

Release resolves a tag/manual reference to an exact commit and tree, enumerates
successful full producers, downloads evidence and requires exactly one unexpired
same-SHA authoritative producer. It verifies the signed manifest against the
repository, signer workflow and source digest, then recomputes every local link.
Missing/expired/ambiguous evidence, changed tags, report/inventory/coverage/build
or producer drift is red. The verification handoff retains SHA, tree, suite digest and complete build-record
digest. Protected promotion re-verifies expiry/tag/tree and
uploads only the already-verified bundle; no build or consumer command runs there.
The fixed AWS adapter obtains an OIDC token, assumes the approved role, uploads
with a SHA-256 checksum, and checks the versioned provider readback checksum and
size. Missing credentials, unsupported provider, skipped upload or mismatched
readback is red.

All actions use immutable full commit pins with version comments. Workflow-level
permissions are empty; test/build jobs get contents-read only. The isolated
non-PR, non-nightly CI signing job alone gets attestations-write and OIDC for
signing. In release, only the protected deployment job gets OIDC. Forks receive no
secrets. Artifacts expire within 7 days (raw diagnostics 3; verified promotion 1).
Replace the environment placeholder only with the approved protected environment.

## Validation and sources

Mandatory: repository-pinned js-yaml 3.15.2 parses both workflows, then executable
workflow simulations invoke the shipped CLI through actual YAML `run` snippets.
Mocks exist only at external executable/artifact/provider boundaries. Mutation
checks cover missing/duplicate/red/retried/quarantined/malformed evidence,
stale/expired/ambiguous producers, count/coverage floors, every digest link, moved
tags, changed argv and rebuild attempts. Optional actionlint was absent on the
phase-34 validation host; it cannot replace these checks. That host's older `gh`
also lacks attestation commands; a real release runner must have current GitHub
CLI support, otherwise release stops with its tool error.

Commands and pins checked 2026-09-05 against official sources:
[Node test runner](https://nodejs.org/api/test.html),
[Vitest CLI](https://vitest.dev/guide/cli.html),
[Playwright CLI](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-cli),
[Flutter testing](https://docs.flutter.dev/testing/overview),
[Gradle test reports](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/java_testing.html),
[Nx CLI](https://nx.dev/docs/reference/nx-commands),
[GitHub attestations](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations),
[gh attestation verification](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify).
Action SHA/version pairs were resolved with `git ls-remote --tags` against the
corresponding official `github.com/actions/<action>` repositories, including the
peeled commit for annotated attestation tags.

name: stack-decision
description: Handle requests phrased as choose stack, mobile stack, or compare frameworks by presenting sourced alternatives without defaults and returning an ADR ruling.
---

# Stack decision

Load `references/matrices.md`. Determine which matrices apply from the approved
PRD answers, then present every row in each applicable matrix unchanged.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, leave repository changes to `greenfield-init` or `brownfield-audit`, and return only `StackDecisionOutput` here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-30.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Selection

Ask exactly one selection question per applicable matrix.
Do not preselect any option before the user answers.
Present the backend matrix ONLY when the PRD answers name an API.

Accept an explicit named option or a request to revisit requirements. Do not
infer a choice from preferences. When the user chooses, ask for or summarize the
reason and confirm it before producing the ruling.
If matrix evidence is unavailable, PRD answers conflict, or the reason is unconfirmed, STOP with `status: unresolved` and name the missing evidence or conflicting answers. Treat selection and STOP behavior as honor-system.

## Callers and ownership

Accept calls from `greenfield-init` for new repositories and from `brownfield-audit` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting. Keep matrices and ADR decision content in this skill and `references/matrices.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * roadmap — the CLI that owns every repo-state transition (arc ROADCODE). Decisions
 * and transitions are CODE here; judgment stays MODEL. Plain Node ESM, one dep (zod).
 *
 * Universal exit-code contract (honesty rail — exit codes never lie):
 *   0  success / clean / the requested state holds
 *   1  usage or configuration error (missing config, unknown/args, not-yet-implemented)
 *   2  check failed / refused / red (the caller cannot narrate around it)
 *   3/4 long-poll verdicts (watch — 1657) · 5 watch UNOBSERVED (2384.2) · capacity's gate
 *   verdict is exit 3 (at capacity) · role resolve's UNJUDGED refusal is exit 2
 *
 * Commands are cli/commands/<name>.mjs default-export async run(argv) → exit code.
 * A command whose module is not present yet is listed in the tree with its owning
 * phase and exits 1 with an honest "not yet implemented" line — the skeleton shows
 * the whole tree, honestly.
 */
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs'
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
import { ConfigError } from '../cli/lib/config.mjs'
import { RoadmapRootError } from '../cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs'

// The full §2 command tree. `phase` is the owning phase and `arc` the arc that owns it
// (default ROADCODE); `sub` lists subcommands for --help. A command becomes MOUNTED the
// moment its module lands.
const TREE = {
  config: { phase: 1655, sub: ['check', 'capabilities --json'], desc: 'load bindings or report read-only protocol capabilities' },
  init: { phase: 1655, sub: ['--config', '--scaffold', '--root <dir>'], desc: 'scaffold the roadmap root + config.json' },
  status: { phase: 1655, sub: ['[root]', '--json'], desc: 'derive the live lane table (absorbs arc-status.mjs)' },
  claim: { phase: 1655, sub: ['[root]', '--count N'], desc: 'atomically reserve the next phase number(s)' },
  arm: { phase: 1655, sub: ['<arcId>', '--inline', '--note', '--base-ref', '--mode'], desc: 'write the .building sidecar; refuse a taken lane' },
  disarm: { phase: 1655, sub: ['<arcId>', '--paused'], desc: 'remove/pause the sidecar; clear .arc-mode; free landed claims' },
  gate: { phase: 1656, sub: ['plan <phase>', 'run <phase>'], desc: 'the gate decision table + mechanical execution' },
  result: { phase: 1656, sub: ['check'], desc: 'PhaseExecutionResult .parse() via the consumer schema' },
  contract: { phase: 1656, sub: ['show --json-schema'], desc: 'emit the PhaseExecutionResult JSON Schema' },
  arc: { phase: 1657, sub: ['next <arcId>', 'land <arcId>'], desc: 'position derivation + the ONE landing engine' },
  watch: { phase: 1657, sub: ['<arcId>', '--once'], desc: 'executor liveness (absorbs executor-watch/liveness)' },
  beacon: { phase: 1737, sub: ['<event> --phase <N>', '--detail', '--log', '--session'], desc: 'typed executor heartbeat (closed vocabulary)' },
  'executor-arm': { phase: 1737, sub: ['<N> --session <id> [--executor-id <id>] [--agent-card <path>] [--force]'], desc: 'write the executor arm file (never unbound; refuses over another executor)' },
  'executor-disarm': { phase: 1737, sub: ['<N> [--force]', '--sweep'], desc: 'remove an executor arm (refuses a live one) / sweep exactly the stale set' },
  phase: { phase: 1657, sub: ['validate <N|file>', 'start <N>', 'curate <N> [--apply] [--groups]', 'land <N>'], desc: 'phase-file validation, start, born-clean curation and the worktree-lane land' },

name: Greenfield CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      base_sha:
        description: Approved previous baseline commit SHA
        required: true
        type: string
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: greenfield-ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
jobs:
  affected:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - id: affected
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: node scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs affected
  plan:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.indices }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before || inputs.base_sha }}
        run: node scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs prepare plan
      - id: plan
        env:
          REQUEST: .ci/plan-request.json
          OUTPUT: .ci/plan.json
        run: node scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs plan "$REQUEST" "$OUTPUT"
      - id: matrix
        run: echo "indices=$(node scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs matrix .ci/plan.json)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: plan-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: .ci/plan.json
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7
  shard:
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        index: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: plan-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: .ci
      - env:
          SHARD_INDEX: ${{ matrix.index }}
        run: node scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs prepare run
      - id: run
        env:
          REQUEST: .ci/run-request.json
          OUTPUT: .ci/reports/shard-${{ matrix.index }}.json
        run: node scripts/ci-shard-plan.mjs run "$REQUEST" "$OUTPUT"
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: shard-${{ matrix.index }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: .ci/reports/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7
      - if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: raw-${{ matrix.index }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: .ci/raw/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3
  fanin:
    if: always() && needs.plan.result == 'success'
    needs: [plan, shard]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0

#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, resolve } from 'node:path'

const args = process.argv.slice(2)
if (args.includes('--help')) {
  console.log('Usage: check-readme-catalog.mjs (--catalog <json> | --project-root <dir>) [--readme <file>]')
  process.exit(0)
}
const value = flag => { const i = args.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined }
const readmePath = resolve(value('--readme') ?? 'README.md')
const fail = message => { console.error(message); process.exitCode = 1 }
if (!existsSync(readmePath)) fail(`nonexistent README: ${readmePath}`)
else {
  const body = readFileSync(readmePath, 'utf8')
  const block = body.match(/<!-- repo-catalog:start -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- repo-catalog:end -->/)?.[1]
  if (!block) fail('malformed README catalog')
  else {
    const tableLines = block.split(/\r?\n/).filter(line => line.trim().startsWith('|'))
    const parsedRows = [...block.matchAll(/^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]*?)\s*\|$/gm)]
    if (parsedRows.length !== tableLines.length || parsedRows.length < 2) fail('malformed README catalog row')
    const rows = parsedRows.slice(2).map(([, name, root]) => ({ name: name.trim(), root: root.trim() }))
    const catalogPath = value('--catalog')
    const projectRoot = value('--project-root')
    let projects
    try {
      if (catalogPath) {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(catalogPath), 'utf8'))
        projects = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.projects
        if (!Array.isArray(projects)) throw new Error('shape')
        for (const project of projects) if (!project?.name || !project?.root || !existsSync(resolve(project.root))) throw new Error(`nonexistent catalog root: ${project?.root}`)
      } else if (projectRoot) {
        const root = resolve(projectRoot)
        if (!existsSync(root)) throw new Error('nonexistent project root')
        let name
        if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'))) name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).name
        else if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'))) name = readFileSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'), 'utf8').match(/^name:\s*([^\s#]+)/m)?.[1]
        else for (const file of ['settings.gradle.kts', 'settings.gradle']) if (existsSync(resolve(root, file))) name ??= readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8').match(/rootProject\.name\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)/)?.[1]
        name ??= basename(root)
        projects = [{ name, root: projectRoot }]
      } else throw new Error('choose --catalog or --project-root')
    } catch (error) { fail(`invalid catalog shape or input: ${error.message}`); projects = null }
    const duplicate = (items, label) => {
      const seen = new Set(); for (const item of items) { if (seen.has(item.name)) fail(`duplicate ${label} name: ${item.name}`); seen.add(item.name) }
    }
    duplicate(rows, 'README')
    if (projects) {
      duplicate(projects, 'catalog')
      const byName = new Map(rows.map(row => [row.name, row]))
      const catalogNames = new Set(projects.map(project => project.name))
      for (const project of projects) if (!byName.has(project.name)) fail(`missing README project: ${project.name} (${project.root})`)
      else if (byName.get(project.name).root !== project.root) fail(`README project path mismatch: ${project.name} (${byName.get(project.name).root} != ${project.root})`)
      for (const row of rows) if (!catalogNames.has(row.name)) fail(`orphan README project: ${row.name} (${row.root})`)
    }
  }
}

content: PreToolUse:Bash says: ugrep-guard: rerouted the grep(s) in this command to GNU grep (/bin/grep -I). `grep` from the Bash tool is NOT GNU grep. Claude Code (>=2.1.117) shadows it with a shell function that re-execs its own binary as the embedded ugrep, whose POSIX engine builds a DFA up front and expands counted repetitions. Two or more counted maxima over a wide class make it track the cross product and allocate WITHOUT BOUND — ~100MB/s, no output, and no SIGPIPE to stop it because it never emits a match, so a downstream `head` will not save you. On 2026-08-22 exactly this shape (`grep -o '[^<>]\{0,120\}retry[^<>]\{0,120\}' design.html` over a minified HTML file with a 91,000-char line) reached 8.9G in ONE process, blew past the session's 8G MemoryHigh with its swap cap full, and livelocked the whole session cgroup for 40 minutes. Upstream: anthropics/claude-code#54394. Measured on that file: GNU grep 0.4s/13MB with the correct answer; ugrep unbounded. Single counted repetitions, narrow classes like [0-9], and maxima under 32 are all fine and are never touched here. Only the regex ENGINE changed, so the match result is the same; the one difference is binary files, which -I keeps skipped exactly as the shim does. Write it this way yourself next time: /bin/grep, -P, or rg.

```json
export const DEFAULT_NAME = 'world'

/**
 * Build a greeting for `name`.
 * - `undefined` (or no argument) greets the default name, `world`.
 * - A blank name (empty or whitespace-only) is rejected with a TypeError.
 */
export function greet(name?: string): string {
  if (name === undefined) return `Hello, ${DEFAULT_NAME}!`
  if (typeof name !== 'string' || name.trim() === '') {
    throw new TypeError('greet(name): name must be a non-blank string')
  }
  return `Hello, ${name}!`
}

/**
 * Thin executable adapter over the greeting API (src/index.ts).
 * Contract: docs/ux-canon.md §Interaction rules.
 */
import { greet } from './index.ts'

const HELP_FLAGS = ['--help', '-h']

const USAGE = [
  'Usage: greenfield-proof [name]',
  '',
  'Print "Hello, <name>!" (default name: world).',
  '',
  'Options:',
  '  -h, --help  Print this usage and exit 0',
  '',
].join('\n')

interface Outcome {
  code: number
  stdout: string
  stderr: string
}

function run(argv: readonly string[]): Outcome {
  // Unknown options are rejected first, so they exit 1 even next to --help.
  const unknown = argv.find((arg) => arg.startsWith('-') && !HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))
  if (unknown !== undefined) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Unknown option: ${unknown}\n${USAGE}` }
  if (argv.some((arg) => HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))) return { code: 0, stdout: USAGE, stderr: '' }
  if (argv.length > 1) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Too many arguments: expected at most one name\n${USAGE}` }
  try {
    return { code: 0, stdout: `${greet(argv[0])}\n`, stderr: '' }
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
    return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `${message}\n${USAGE}` }
  }
}

const outcome = run(process.argv.slice(2))
process.stdout.write(outcome.stdout)
process.stderr.write(outcome.stderr)
process.exitCode = outcome.code
'''

## Visual language

None. The product has no graphical surface; the only user interface is plain CLI text on stdout and stderr, with no colours, tokens, fonts, palette or spacing.

- Greeting line: `Hello, <name>!` followed by a newline on stdout.

| Invocation | stdout | stderr | exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `greenfield-proof ''` or a whitespace-only name | empty | the `TypeError` message + usage | 1 |
| more than one name | empty | `Too many arguments` + usage | 1 |
```

```json
 * Reusable greeting API. The CLI in ./cli.ts is a thin adapter over this module.
 * Contract: docs/ux-canon.md §Interaction rules.

export const DEFAULT_NAME = 'world'

/**
 * Build a greeting for `name`.
 * - `undefined` (or no argument) greets the default name, `world`.
 * - A blank name (empty or whitespace-only) is rejected with a TypeError.
 */
export function greet(name?: string): string {
  if (name === undefined) return `Hello, ${DEFAULT_NAME}!`
  if (typeof name !== 'string' || name.trim() === '') {
    throw new TypeError('greet(name): name must be a non-blank string')
  }
  return `Hello, ${name}!`

CONTENT['src/cli.ts'] = r'''#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * Thin executable adapter over the greeting API (src/index.ts).
 * Contract: docs/ux-canon.md §Interaction rules.
 */
import { greet } from './index.ts'

const HELP_FLAGS = ['--help', '-h']

const USAGE = [
  'Usage: greenfield-proof [name]',
  '',
  'Print "Hello, <name>!" (default name: world).',
  '',
  'Options:',
  '  -h, --help  Print this usage and exit 0',
  '',
].join('\n')

interface Outcome {
  code: number
  stdout: string
  stderr: string
}

function run(argv: readonly string[]): Outcome {
  // Unknown options are rejected first, so they exit 1 even next to --help.
  const unknown = argv.find((arg) => arg.startsWith('-') && !HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))
  if (unknown !== undefined) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Unknown option: ${unknown}\n${USAGE}` }
  if (argv.some((arg) => HELP_FLAGS.includes(arg))) return { code: 0, stdout: USAGE, stderr: '' }
  if (argv.length > 1) return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `Too many arguments: expected at most one name\n${USAGE}` }
  try {
    return { code: 0, stdout: `${greet(argv[0])}\n`, stderr: '' }
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)
    return { code: 1, stdout: '', stderr: `${message}\n${USAGE}` }
  }
}

const outcome = run(process.argv.slice(2))
process.stdout.write(outcome.stdout)
process.stderr.write(outcome.stderr)
process.exitCode = outcome.code

## Visual language

None. The product has no graphical surface; the only user interface is plain CLI text on stdout and stderr, with no colours, tokens, fonts, palette or spacing.

## Component vocabulary

- Greeting line: `Hello, <name>!` followed by a newline on stdout.
- Usage text: starts with `Usage: greenfield-proof [name]` and lists the options.
- Error line: one sentence on stderr, followed by the usage text.

## Interaction rules

| Invocation | stdout | stderr | exit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `greenfield-proof` | `Hello, world!` | empty | 0 |
| `greenfield-proof Ada` | `Hello, Ada!` | empty | 0 |
| `greenfield-proof --help` or `-h` | usage text | empty | 0 |
| `greenfield-proof --unknown` | empty | `Unknown option: --unknown` + usage | 1 |
| `greenfield-proof --help --unknown` (any order) | empty | `Unknown option: --unknown` + usage | 1 |
| `greenfield-proof ''` or a whitespace-only name | empty | the `TypeError` message + usage | 1 |
| more than one name | empty | `Too many arguments` + usage | 1 |

Unknown options are checked before help, so an unknown option never exits 0. The API mirrors the CLI: `greet()` and `greet(undefined)` return `Hello, world!`, `greet(name)` returns `Hello, <name>!` verbatim, and blank names throw `TypeError`.

none — ADR 0002 records the non-UI ruling; `designHomes.ux.bindingDesignSystem` is absent and no tokens are defined.
```
